title: King Arthur's Original Cake Pan Cake
description: Over the years, Cake Pan Cake has become one of our most beloved recipes — and for good reason. Named for its original no-bowl method (traditionally, everything was mixed right in the pan), this iconic chocolate cake traces its roots to the Great Depression, when clever, resourceful bakers created rich desserts without butter, eggs, or milk. The result is a pantry-friendly, affordable, and delightfully easy cake that’s moist and tender with deep chocolate flavor — perfect for kids, beginners, and anyone who loves a low-effort, high-reward bake. While the classic chocolate version is the most celebrated (it was our 2014 Recipe of the Year), we’ve since created other variations (vanilla, lemon, and spice), proving that this humble dessert truly is a cake for all bakers.

ingredients.name: King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour
ingredients.raw: 1 1/2 cups (180g) King Arthur Unbleached All-Purpose Flour

ingredients.name: unsweetened cocoa, Dutch-process or natural*
ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup (21g) unsweetened cocoa, Dutch-process or natural*

ingredients.name: cider vinegar or white vinegar
ingredients.raw: 1 tablespoon (14g) cider vinegar or white vinegar

ingredients.name: King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract
ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon King Arthur Pure Vanilla Extract

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Lightly grease an 8" square or 9" round pan that's at least 2" deep.
To make the cake: In a medium bowl, whisk together the dry ingredients.
In a separate bowl, whisk together {i7}, oil, {i9}, and vanilla. Pour the wet ingredients into the bowl of dry ingredients, stirring until thoroughly combined. Pour the batter into the prepared pan.

Bake the cake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, or with a few moist crumbs clinging to it. The cake can be served right from the pan, still warm, at this point; or allow the cake to cool while you prepare the icing.

To make the chocolate icing: In a medium heatproof bowl, combine {i11} and {i12}. Heat in the microwave in 30-second increments, stirring between each, until the chocolate melts. (Alternatively, this can be done in a small saucepan over low heat.) Stir the icing until smooth and then pour/spread over the cake. Allow the icing to set briefly before slicing and serving.
Storage information: Store leftover cake, well covered, at room temperature for several days; freeze for longer storage.
